Meh, not a huge fan of it as is, but I'm withholding judgement until I actually feel the final product in my hand for a number of reasons:

  • I have been surprised by controllers in the past (Wii U Gamepad and DS included)
  • Almost any controller, unless it is extremely poorly designed, can be fine if it's used right. Not to mention Nintendo is good at using unique hardware effectively.
  • Controllers change through development. The Wii U Gampad originally looked like an iPad with two Wii Remotes and Circle Pads taped to the side.
  • Nintendo hasn't released a console that lacks backwards compatibility with previous controllers in over a decade. Even the Wii had a traditional controller available early on and the Wii U supports Gamecube controllers in a limited sense..
  • In the age of consumer 3D printers, there is a far greater chance of this being complete bullshit than ever before.

I could actually see this being comfortable if done right or being a total disaster if botched. Until the public and developers get their hands on it there is just no way to tell.
